Hierarchy 1 description en: A resource comprising of a group of items the parts of which may be separately described and navigated. [DC]

Hierarchy 2 description en: A collection of items presented in a protective folder.
Structured descriptions of an archive or collection used to assist retrieval and management, or presentation to the public.

Hierarchy 3 description en: Structured list of information about items of interest to a research project, for example monuments of a particular type.

Hierarchy 4 alternative en: Organised and documented collection of the records that collectively provide information on sites and monuments (ie site forms, site sheets, finds catalogues, etc)

Hierarchy 2 description en: Collection of artefacts recovered during archaeological investigation of a site.
Collection of information on sites and monuments held by a single resercher in their archives (in analogue and/or digital format)
Documents relating to the administration of planning applications.
Organised and documented collection of the records made during the course of a project.

Hierarchy 1 description en: Information encoded in a defined structure (for example, lists, tables, and databases), intended to be useful for direct machine processing. [DC] For manual data use index, gazetteer etc.

Hierarchy 2 description en: Data suitable for processing using computer aided design (CAD) packages.
Data suitable for processing using database management software.
Machine readable files suitable for use in a geographic information system (GIS).

Hierarchy 3 description en: Geospatial data on sites location and characteristics that have been identified through remote sensing techniques
Geospatial data on sites location and characteristics that have been identified throughfield survey and have been recorded using a tablet or other electronic device

Hierarchy 1 description en: A visual representation of a physical object, place or person. [DC] Use a more specific term where appropriate.

Hierarchy 2 description en: A pictoral depiction of an area of landscape.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A depiction of land, coastal or sea areas intended to aid navigation, usually using latitude and longitude co-ordinates.
A map generally produced manually to indicate main features of an area quickly, for example to assist location of a particular place.

Hierarchy 2 description en: Broad term for all types of animated or live action images.

Hierarchy 3 description en: Recording of a complete broadcast television programme, for instance a documentary. For extracts such as items from news broadcasts use VIDEO CLIP.
An extract from a longer video film, used as an illustration.

Hierarchy 2 description en: An image created by controlled exposure of light sensitive film. Usually a static image in time and space. For digital photographs double index with an appropriate term under MACHINE READABLE STORAGE MEDIUM.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A photograph taken from the air.

Hierarchy 4 alternative en: An aerial photograph taken at an angle other than 90 degrees to a feature in the landscape.

An aerial photograph taken from directly above a feature in the landscape, suitable for mapping or survey purposes. For photographs taken from the air at an angle to the subject use OBLIQUE AERIAL PHOTOGRAPH.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A photograph usually of a standing structure that has been manipulated to allow the creation of a measured drawing of the facade or elevation.

Hierarchy 2 description en: General term for images used to represent a particular place or item, or convey information.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A manually produced image for illustration or record purposes.

Hierarchy 4 alternative en: A drawn representation of an archaeological 'find' or other cultural object.
A representation of a monument or landscape based on historical or archaeological information.
A plan of a feature or small area generally done in the field to quickly record the main features.
A broad class of drawing that is produced following precise conventions of scale and projection. [AAT]

Hierarchy 5 description en: The process of transcribing the features on an aerial photograph onto a map or plan.
A schematic depiction of the results of an archaeological excavation.

Hierarchy 6 description en: Scale drawing showing the horizontal extent, height and arrangement of an excavated layer or feature on an archaeological site.
Drawing of the vertical face of an excavated feature or features depicting the vertical extent and stratigraphic relationship between identified layers or deposits.

Hierarchy 5 description en: Plan showing a horizontal section, size and arrangement of rooms within a building, may include location of doors, windows and other features.
A drawing which depicts to scale a feature within the landscape. For drawings of selected features of a site use SCALE DRAWING..
A drawing, generally on a transparent sheet, which can be placed on top of another image to combine information from both.
Used for orthographic drawings in the horizontal plane, generally from above generally depicts localised areas.
A scaled drawing based on measurements taken from life.
A schematic diagram showing the relationships of the composition and strata of layers identified during excavation or intervention.
A drawing used to convey information about the arrangement and size of features in a defined location under study.

Hierarchy 3 description en: An image used to convey information, often as part of a larger publication or exhibition.
Reproduced image derived by mechanical printing from an image engraved or carved on a suitable surface.

Hierarchy 4 alternative en: An image produced by creating marks on a hard material from which a print is then taken.
A relief process in which the design is cut into and printed from the plank side of a wood block [AAT].

Hierarchy 3 description en: An image created manually using paint or pigments, to record, illustrate or convey impressions.
Card printed with an image, often a photograph on one side, and space for a short message and a postal address on the other.
A drawing, often made in the field as the basis for later work, or to quickly convey important information.

Hierarchy 1 description en: A resource which requires interaction from the user to be understood, executed, or experienced. [DC]

Hierarchy 2 description en: Materials selected and organised to be of use to teachers for use in education.
A file of computer information stored on a computer connected to the internet coded so that it can be accessed over the internet using browser software.

Hierarchy 1 description en: A service is a system that provides one or more functions of value to the end-user. Examples include: a photocopying service, a banking service, an authentication service, inter-library loans, a Z39.50 or Web server. [DC]

Hierarchy 2 description en: A database stored on a computer linked to the internet, which can be queried and browsed by remote users using the internet.

Hierarchy 1 description en: A sound is a resource whose content is primarily intended to be rendered as audio. [DC] For example recorded speech, sounds or music.

Hierarchy 2 description en: Recorded interview intended to preserve the recollections of persons whose experiences or memories are representative of historical life.
Recording of a complete broadcast radio programme.

Hierarchy 1 description en: A resource whose content is primarily words for reading. For example - books, letters, dissertations, poems, newspapers, articles, archives of mailing lists. [DC]

Hierarchy 2 description en: Written communication, generally in the form of letters.
A chronological journal, generally showing appointments, or recording memories and impressions of a days events over a period of time.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A diary used to record the events and activities during an excavation.

Hierarchy 2 description en: A structured set of data taken from a larger work to assist in location of particular subject matter.

Hierarchy 3 description en: Cards, often printed with forms, for the recording and sorting of information in a structured manner.

Hierarchy 2 description en: An unpublished document.
Book used to record information or impressions in the field, often as a preparation for more formal reporting at a later date.

This term is appropriate to official notifications of a monument or area whether they are statutory or purely advisory. Where possible the specific document type should be indexed for example Scheduled Monument Notification.

Hierarchy 3 description en: The contents of these documents do not confer any statutory designation on the monuments listed, they are purely advisory notifications for use within preserving the historic environment.

A list of English battlefields maintained by English Heritage. Inclusion in the document does not confer any statutory status. It lists and records the details of battlefields to preserve their nature and survival.

A register which including sites retaining any evidence of pre-1750 layouts; significant evidence of pre-1820 layouts; good examples of the best gardens from 1820 to 1880; are good examples of the best gardens laid out after 1880 but before 1970.

Hierarchy 2 description en: Copy of a single article or section from a serial or monograph taken from the same printing as the original.
This class of documents confers statutory designation on the monuments listed within them. It usually is restricted to legally defined national or local notifications of designation.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A list of buildings of special architectural or historic interest. This list confers a statutory level of protection status to the buildings contained within it and usually includes a description of each building.

Hierarchy 3 en: List of gazetted sites and monuments
Hierarchy 3 description en: A list of archaeological sites and monuments of special interest. This list confers a statutory level of protection status to the sites and monuments contained within it and usually includes a description of each site.

Any notification, update or amendment relating to the scheduling/gazeeting of a monument. Usually includes description and a map showing the limit of the scheduling. It confers a statutory status and receipt is an acknowledgement of the scheduling.

Hierarchy 2 description en: Written copy of recorded interviews collected to illustrate history from personal experiences.
General term for documents that have been produced in large numbers for public sale or distribution.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A written work for publication, being one of several found in a serial, monograph or magazine.

Hierarchy 4 alternative en: A written extract taken from a published newspaper.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A complete written work. Includes books and anthologies.
A book containing information about a place that has been produced for the use of visitors or tourists.
A short published document, often a single sheet, describing a particular place, feature or service to assist visitors and users.
Publication on a specific topic, or limited scope of subject matter. Complete in itself, though may form part of a series.
Short publication used to disseminate information about a particular project or organisation, issued on a regular basis.
A written work issued at regular intervals, numbered consecutively with no intended or planned end point.
A written work issued in parts, with the intention of creating a completed sequence.
A bound written work.

Hierarchy 2 description en: A paper form used to record specific information in a systematic way.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A form used to record the details of a feature identified by archaeological investigation, generally including location, depth, colour, texture, inclusions and stratigraphic relationship to other contexts.
A form to record the details of a monument or site found during the course of a field survey or visit.
A form that records the details of a project, for example, an excavation index form.

Hierarchy 2 description en: A full written presentation of the details of a particular event or investigative technique, often including illustrations and appendices.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A report detailing the results of the application of scientific techniques to the analysis of archaeological materials.
A report detailing the results of a study of the fabric of a standing building.
A report providing an objective analysis of the elements which together define the special architectural or historic interest of a specific area.
A report on the archaeology of an area, based primarily on existing records and resources.
A report detailing the results of an archaeological excavation.
A report detailing the results of an archaeological evaluation
A report detailing the results of a field survey. Usually restricted to a survey of a small or specific area or site.
A report detailing the results of an archaeological event were the ground surface has been studied and any visible archaeological material collected.
A report that primarily details the results of a survey that was conducted using remote sensing techniques such as resistivity and magnetometry.
A report detailing subsurface investigations conducted to assist with the technical rather than archaeological aspects of a proposed development or extraction scheme.
A report detailing the archaeological and architectural potential of a site or locality.
A report depicting the results generated from an intensive survey of a large area of land including field recording, measured site surveys and land history.
A report detailing the results of archaeological fieldwork that has been produced in advance of a full synthesis of the collected data.
A report which represents an initial synthesis of the data collected from an excavation ahead of the production of a full publication/post excavation full analysis report.
A report which represents the final assessment and analysis of an archaeological intervention.
An outline of the circumstances to be addressed, with an indication of the scope of work which will be required (English term)

A schedule of work set out in sufficient detail for it to be quantifiable, implemented and monitored. Can include contractual details relevant to the commissioning body. A project design may be a research proposal independent of the planning framework
An outline of the circumstances to be addressed, with an indication of the scope of work which will be required (Scottish term)
A schedule of work in sufficient detail for it to be quantifiable, implemented and monitored.
A report that primarily details the results of attempts to assign a date to materials or deposits using scientific methods such as Palaeomagnetism, Dendrochronology or Radiocarbon Dating.

Hierarchy 4 description en: A report that primarily details the results of attempts to assign a date to wooden structures or objects by the comparative study of the growth rings in trees and aged wood.
A report that primarily details the results of attempts to assign a date to orgainic material by measuring the amount of carbon 14 it contains.

Hierarchy 3 description en: A report written as a result of archaeological monitoring during development work.

Hierarchy 2 description en: A book in which visitors to a property, monument or exhibition record their thoughts and impressions on their experience.

Hierarchy 1 description en: Factual information conveyed orally to a recipient. Where this has been transcribed, use an appropriate term from the TEXT hierarchy.
